item.title: Brain’s Developmental Switch May Shape Lifelong Obesity Risk
item.description: Is your weight gain pre-programmed? Scientists have discovered a developmental "fate-switch" in the brain that decides if you’ll be driven by hunger or fullness.

item.title: Mother-Child Brainwave Syncing Defeats the Language Barrier
item.description: Language doesn't limit love. New brain imaging research reveals that bilingual mothers and their children stay perfectly "in sync" even when speaking a second language.

item.title: Mapping Technology Reveals the Brain’s Secret Protein Factories
item.description: DNA is just the beginning. A new mapping technology reveals that brain cells produce proteins at wildly different rates, providing a missing link in our understanding of neurological disease.

item.title: Social Competition Can Turn Nurturing Dads into Neglectful Ones
item.description: Is neglect a molecular choice? Scientists have discovered a brain switch that can turn a "Dad-of-the-Year" into a neglectful parent based on his environment.

item.title: Why Some Brains Are Biologically Unable to Process Loss
item.description: Grief shouldn't be a life sentence. Researchers are uncovering why some brains get "stuck" in a cycle of craving and longing after the loss of a loved one.

item.title: Sleep Protects the Brain’s Powerhouses from Toxic Waste
item.description: Think of sleep as a janitorial shift. New research reveals how slumber protects your brain’s powerhouses by hauling away toxic waste produced during the day.

item.title: Electronic Mesh Wraps Around Mini-Brains to Eavesdrop on Neural Circuits
item.description: It’s a high-tech hug for your brain cells. Scientists have developed a "pop-up" electronic mesh that wraps around mini-brains to map every spark and signal.

item.title: Hacking Musical Chills: Triggering Peak Musical Pleasure
item.description: Hack your goosebumps. A new brain-music interface uses in-ear sensors to read your emotions and curate a playlist that guarantees peak "musical chills."

item.title: New Human Neuron Networks Decode Developing Brain Rhythms
item.description: Researchers have developed a high-speed "neuron-on-a-plate" system that successfully mimics the complex electrical rhythms of the developing human brain.

item.title: Less Experience Leads to Faster Neural Adaptation
item.description: A new study finds that the brain learns better from spaced-out, rare events than from constant repetition, challenging 100 years of Pavlovian theory.
